**Verified 2026-10-12 live GitHub:** [research/issue-381-d4-s1](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/tree/bb46ba8bd0d4a2a01af976fb9b05d6c4224b4697) HEAD `bb46ba8bd0d4a2a01af976fb9b05d6c4224b4697`, exact Tree `501bc4e54d9a391625888e4aab3485119e971f4b`, parent D4-S0 `b86fa298441729f7cb0027e076aa3d34a3d3ac04`, 1 commit / 12 files entirely in `docs/project/research/issue-381-d4-s1/`. Research is **accepted as a solid proposed architecture and source audit**, with textual/inferred inventory limitations stated correctly. No independent execution of generators/tests by Owner; no full CI/Hosted needed for a doc-only proposal.

**Direction approved for continued design:** *Root Membership + Effective Visibility* as **the preferred logical managed-file visibility authority**, with source-path entry, per-root complete generation membership and single manifest-pointer CAS; positive root membership prevents cross-root false stale. Preserve user edits/history; missing vs unmanaged vs uncertainty/legacy distinct; Global Index remains independent. Adopt all-or-nothing atomic publication **for the explicitly included effective roots of one session**; a failed root preserves previous head and any subset retry must be a separate explicitly scoped operation with clear UI result. Legacy non-stale unknown rows remain discoverable in a visibly labeled read-only compatibility slice; no automated missing or destructive action absent proven ownership/re-identification and explicit user authorization.

**Critical physical schema blocker not resolved in ADR: path reuse and historical incarnation.** Frozen Schema37 `files` has `path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, user tags `file_user_tags.file_id REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, and similar file-linked fingerprint/duplicate/content relations. `scan.rs::upsert_file_rows_tx` uses `INSERT INTO files ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE` and resets `is_stale=0`. The ADR promises to keep old source/history and create a *distinct source incarnation* when a **new file occupies the same path**, but never defines a collision-safe mapping between immutable `source_id` and mutable `files.id/path`. Simply inserting another base row violates UNIQUE(path); updating/recycling the old row risks silent metadata/tag/analysis inheritance; deleting the old row cascades. A stable source ID alone does not resolve this. **Before any production implementation, show a complete Schema37-compatible old/new incarnation + rename + hardlink + FK/trigger/FTS transition with retained historical links**, choosing one explicit physical schema strategy and migration/compatibility cost. Require deterministic idempotent upgrade/recovery proof on synthetic Schema37 databases.

**Further required ADR amendments:**
1. **Identity / ownership:** distinguish path-entry incarnation, verified physical file identity, rename/move equivalence, hardlink aliases, inode/file-id reuse, path-only/unsupported identity, root changed/detached and ACL/reparse boundaries; record which facts authorize *presence* and *absence* separately. A missing OS identity must never silently authenticate old source reuse or metadata transfer.
2. **Legacy/action conflict:** ADR §4.2 says legacy is 'read-only for destructive operations until an action-boundary identity check succeeds', whereas §4.3 says unassigned/ambiguous legacy cannot override missing ownership. Resolve in one fail-closed rule: **an identity check alone cannot manufacture root membership or grant destructive authority**; explicit user selection plus native authorization/identity proof and an owned-source transition may be separately designed. Mark compatibility badges/tokens; preserve all historical associations.
3. **Read/mutate completeness:** inventory is line-based nearest-function heuristic, not exhaustive Rust/SQL call graph. Assign an owner and oracle assertion for every by-ID/detail/path/FTS/snippet/tag count/duplicate/content/AI/proposal/Global bridge as well as SQL triggers and frontend actions. Define revision domains including user metadata independent of root membership, active-state filtering, writer commit CAS and cross-transaction cursor expiry. No dual authorities or direct `files.is_stale` product writes after activation.
4. **FTS/ranking:** define whether BM25 corpus includes hidden legacy/stale files and what rank ordering is required. FTS postfilter may hide rows but not remove their document-frequency contribution to BM25. Run **small, plan-only / correctness-only** paired exact-bundled-SQLite 3.51.3 SQL comparison, no performance gate inferred from host 3.53.1 or D4-S0 page measurement. Large benchmark needs later permission.
5. **Completeness, cost, durability:** spell out count+digest identity/evidence encoding, root-scope and watcher watermarks under disjoint source mutations, multi-root parent CAS, bounded retries, immutability and stage GC references; bound staged positive-membership write amplification, WAL/disk/pinned historical reader pressure, fail-closed OS->SQLite race and its postpublication repair. Do not assume a logical cursor lease holds a SQLite WAL snapshot across transactions.
6. **#380 prerequisite:** Installer/IPC/DB-generation isolation unproven; Schema 38 unallocated. Any old client writing `files.is_stale` into a migrated DB must be blocked *before* pointer authority is enabled. **Verified on GitHub (2026-10-12):** `research/issue-381-d4-s2` HEAD `0a29c5b0114744f810de90ad31146394ce7be399`, Tree `7de3c7478868dd17b53884e9481d1d6ce60b7b99`, direct parent D4-S1 `bb46ba8bd0d4a2a01af976fb9b05d6c4224b4697` (Tree `501bc4e54d9a391625888e4aab3485119e971f4b`), one commit / 9 changed files exclusively under `docs/project/research/issue-381-d4-s2/`. Frozen master remains `3275ac7c72df8ae4139a30f16c7f649971324e97` (Tree `009576241cd4e8e2ba12cc644a368314f599faa6`). PR #383 OPEN/Draft at `584621c32054e16ac0a61afc669a04380a976b7f`; PR #386 OPEN/Draft at `d260131f9d6ec354f2361e6c7460c79e62e38391`. Schema v38 unallocated.

Read full ADR amendment, MIGRATION-TRUTH-TABLE, VALIDATION-CONTRACT, 294-line SQL, 983-line Python Harness, evidence JSON, SHA manifest, and baseline Schema37 constraints. The committed JSON reports SQLite 3.53.1, 15 listed assertion groups passing, unchanged original table row/value digests over 13 tables (one synthetic row in each of most related tables), no unexpected direct files(id) FK changes, FTS external-content integrity, DDL failure rollback, forced process exit before COMMIT and successful restart/redo. The Harness source contains corresponding `assert` statements; Owner **did not independently execute the Harness**. Results entries are a summary dictionary emitted after those assertions, not 15 separately executed production qualification suites; the comparison covers a small synthetic fixture only.

**Approved logical/physical direction for further design (not a physical production schema freeze):** retain legacy `files.id` and `rowid` as stable FK/FTS anchors; remove uniqueness of `files.path` in a coordinated rebuild; introduce immutable opaque `source_id`, durable file/source crosswalk and append-only path entries; distinguish verified hard links, path reuse, renames and explicit legacy user claims; represent root-owned complete generation membership and select a per-manifest derived effective-path projection with a single pointer CAS. Never automatically transfer old notes/tags/content/fingerprints/AI by same path. This is demonstrably more viable than recycling old `files.id` or deleting user associations.

**Blocking invariants discovered by direct source inspection:**

1. **Manifest projection completeness and identity proof are not enforced.** `harness/run.py::create_manifest` accepts independent `root_generations` and caller-supplied `projections`; `manifest_file_paths` constraints enforce *no duplicate paths / no double paths per source*, but NOT equality between (a) union of all selected, complete root-generation members and (b) all selected projection rows, nor exact `path_key`, `projected_path`, `path_entry_id` / identity-digest provenance. A manifest omitting a valid source or swapping a path projection to unobserved evidence may still be pointer-selected. `effective_file_sources` applies a membership inner join, which filters some unmatched projections but does **not detect incomplete projection**: undercount/hide without a valid stale decision remains possible. Require independent set-equality oracle (both EXCEPT directions), count+canonical digest, source/path identity and root/session/watcher fences checked **inside pointer publication**, with negative tests that leave the old pointer unchanged.
2. **“Immutable published generation/manifest” is descriptive, not enforced by current SQL.** Only `file_path_entries` have UPDATE and guarded DELETE triggers; `source_generation_members`, `source_generations`, `manifest_root_heads`, `manifest_file_paths`, `visibility_manifests` lack equivalent post-ready/post-published immutability protections. After pointer commit an UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT on referenced rows can alter effective visibility with **no pointer revision change**; this violates cursor, job and historical snapshot guarantees. Define immutable status transitions, strict published-reference guards, safe stage insertion/projection completion, and negative post-publish mutation tests. Do not rely solely on developer discipline or SQLite unique indexes.
3. **Retained historical FTS versus manifest-bound reads remains unresolved.** In the Harness a same-object rename directly `UPDATE files.path/name` before pointer COMMIT; the external-content FTS updates current tokens. The active `effective_file_sources` view follows the singleton *current* manifest, not a caller-pinned historical `manifest_id`. A durable cross-transaction cursor/reader lease for an old manifest cannot simply replay historic path/name/FTS semantics from mutated `files` + current FTS; stale BM25 global corpus/IDF is likewise unresolved. Define whether cursors on publication flip always fail stale-token vs leased historical generation, and prove matching list/detail/path/FTS/snippet/rank semantics. A logical manifest lease is **not** a SQLite WAL snapshot lease. Keep #381 FTS3.51.3 exact-build plan+correctness gate; no 10k/100k timing yet.
4. **Direct source-index and legacy writers still need a coordinated cutover.** Schema37 Scanner uses path as `files.id`, and numerous writers/readers still assume one row per path or raw `files.is_stale`. Removing `UNIQUE(path)` **cannot ship alone**. A migration must atomically switch every managed writer/reader, by-ID lookup, FTS/trigger side-effect and old-client gate, not merely preserve foreign keys. `source_gc_authorizations` / deletion triggers test that unauthorized delete fails, but do **not** constitute a completed, history-aware GC proof.
5. **Evidence availability gap:** `evidence/SHA256SUMS` and `INPUTS.json` reference `docs/project/research/issue-381-d4-s2/evidence/schema37-physical-harness-run.log` SHA `317ccfe4bd885746d8ded808dcdc96c0ef117c57bc12631a7c2808fd84067f06`, but this file returns GitHub 404 at exact S2 HEAD and is absent from the 9-file diff. JSON result and full Harness source are accessible; do **not** claim the run log is independently remotely archived. Rectify by committing exact log if preserved, or explicitly marking unavailable and removing stale manifest claim; never fabricate/reconstruct an “original” run log.

Other explicit limits: captured Schema37 DDL plus synthetic rows are not a real old-user DB; Python-linked SQLite 3.53.1 is not exact product SQLite 3.51.3; native Windows/macOS filesystem identity/reparse/ACL, watcher completeness, DB upgrade, mixed-generation client/Service isolation, disk/WAL scale remain unproven. #380 remains cross-track hard dependency, with no migration version allocated and no PR merges.

**Next authorization: D4-S3 FOCUSED AUTHORITY-PROOF REMEDIATION (research/test-only GO).** In a separate research-only successor from exact D4-S2 HEAD:
- Resolve evidence manifest/run-log discrepancy without altering or pretending a new run log is historical.
- Amend SQL *prototype* and validation contract to require frozen published manifests, root generations and members; insert/update/delete/delete-cascade negative tests; stage-to-published transitions and recovery rules.
- Add a small standalone, deterministic **counterexample-first** Harness using actual D4-S2 SQL: construct (i) incomplete projection, (ii) wrong path/path-entry evidence, (iii) extra phantom projection, (iv) post-publication member/head/projection changes, (v) stale cross-transaction cursor/list/detail/FTS read. Demonstrate old candidate fails at least once, then protect with explicit set equality and pointer-commit validation. Preserve accepted old 15 assertions. No mocks claiming real watcher/native identity.
- Decide and specify **one** explicit cursor policy (recommended initially: reject stale cross-transaction tokens; short reads use pinned SQLite transaction), not unproven durable old FTS replay. Retain history through a separate historical API. Define BM25 effective-corpus requirement for future FTS qualification.
- Provide exact frozen-schema-source read/write migration coverage and #380 old-client/DB-generation barrier in the combined migration ADR (still a proposal). Do NOT change product code, PR #383/#386, master, schema number, installer, IPC, CI, timeouts or any Hosted Windows/macOS run.

Do not start full CI or broad benchmarks; only small offline SQLite research tests may run. Preserve exact HEAD/Tree, raw outputs, reproducibility and negative-evidence SHA manifest. Stop at `#381-D4-S3 READY_FOR_OWNER_AUTHORITY_PROOF_REVIEW` if scoped invariants are demonstrated, else `#381-D4-S3 MANIFEST_AUTHORITY_UNRESOLVED`. Neither state authorizes D4 production implementation or merger of PR #383. No Codex Review, merge, issue close, release.

**Disposition:** `#381-D4-S2 PHYSICAL_STORAGE_FEASIBILITY_ACCEPTED / MANIFEST_COMPLETENESS_UNPROVEN / PRODUCTION_NO_GO / D4-S3_RESEARCH_ONLY_GO`.

Independently fetched/reviewed [ADR-002](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/blob/ad85df097d7a8425df01e1a95829c38fd17dd4d6/docs/project/research/issue-381-d4-s3/ADR-002-unified-manifest-authority.md), [SQL-ORACLE](https://github.com/ArdenZC/Zen-Canvas/blob/ad85df097d7a8425df01e1a95829c38fd17dd4d6/docs/project/research/issue-381-d4-s3/SQL-ORACLE.md), both proposed SQL files, 914-line Python runner, source-backed JSON, contract, provenance, SHA manifest and recovered original D4-S2 run log. Scope correct. Research's test results are supported by corresponding source assertions, **but Owner did not independently re-execute** the harness. The archived D4-S2 run log is present on this exact commit (absent from frozen S2 tree as previously noted), listed with its previously reported SHA `317ccfe4bd885746d8ded808dcdc96c0ef117c57bc12631a7c2808fd84067f06`; preserving original provenance rather than retroactively claiming S2 included it is correct.

### Accepted core evidence

- D4-S2 original 15 assertions are reused by import/run (not merely transcribed).
- Seven old-model counterexamples cover missing projection, wrong path, phantom projection, invalid identity, post-publication member UPDATE/DELETE without pointer revision, and cross-transaction Cursor misuse.
- Four protected illegal publication types fail closed. Two bidirectional `EXCEPT` operations now run in the **manifest status publication trigger** and are independently reported by the Oracle. Valid nested-root dedup yields expected=actual=1 with matching digest.
- SQL DML triggers reject 16 mutation attempts across the five published tables/pointer: `source_generation_members`, `source_generations`, `manifest_root_heads`, `manifest_file_paths`, `visibility_manifests`; CAS revision also guarded. The research demonstration preserves original pointer and visible source after rejected mutations.
- Failed rename transaction reverts changed `files` payload/FTS tokens, new path entry and pointer. Successful rename publishes together with FTS, immutable path history retained, prior WAL snapshot remains coherent, old **cross-transaction Cursor explicitly rejects**; no unsupported historical FTS replay.
- Small SQLite 3.53.1 FTS experiment shows raw 2 / visible 1, so current `bm25(files_fts)` continues to use hidden corpus stats; correctly left as a production blocker.

**This clears the explicitly scoped D4-S2 missing/extra projection and five-table post-publish DML blockers. The physical source-incarnation direction and Manifest/Cursor conceptual architecture can now be frozen as a preferred *design basis*, not a production schema or implementation gate.**

### Important remaining authority-boundary blockers found in source

**A. Referential / transitive published-evidence mutability (high priority).** The D4-S3 freeze triggers cover five specific tables, **not** mutable records referenced by that authority: `scan_runs.status/coverage_complete`, `file_sources.status/identity_confidence/source_revision`, `file_physical_identity_epochs.identity_epoch/platform_file_identity/evidence_digest`, `source_identity_claims`, and `scan_roots` path/coverage definitions. The publish trigger checks the first four sets of fields, but D4-S3 has no post-publication DML guards/revision fences for these referenced rows. E.g. a compatible process could change a referenced `scan_runs.coverage_complete` or `file_sources.identity_confidence` after publication without pointer revision; `effective_file_sources` itself only joins crosswalk and member/projection, so existing visibility can persist under invalidated identity evidence. These inputs must either be sealed for the lifetime of every referencing published manifest **or** cause an atomic pointer/revision invalidation through the one authorized write path. Show direct-SQL negative tests for update/delete of each dependency and a documented revision model. Do not mistakenly freeze independent user tag/metadata edits that must remain allowed under their own CAS domain.

**B. Declarative digest vs enforced digest (high priority).** `run.py::oracle_report` recomputes SHA256 root-map and `source_generation_members` digests inside a transaction, but `manifest-authority-protection.sql::d4s3_manifest_publish_guard` checks only generation **member count**, coverage and set/identity consistency; it does **not** compare `sg.member_digest` or `vm.root_map_digest` to a recomputed value. SQLite lacks a native SHA256 UDF in this Harness, as the ADR admits. Thus the SQL guard alone is not a complete cryptographic commitment; a direct `UPDATE visibility_manifests SET status='published'` with a valid exact projection but incorrect digest may be accepted if it bypasses the checked publication routine. Do not claim that all invariant checks are trigger-enforced. Define a single callable, locked, version-gated publication authority and protect against direct status/pointer writes outside it (or state/validate an equivalent narrow trusted-writer assumption). Add a negative bypass test and exact encoding/version contract for the production language and SQLite release. The S3 model successfully proves *set equality at publication*, not unconditionally tamper-proof digest authority.

**C. External frontiers remain explicit NO-GO:** current native source identity, watcher revision/gap and filesystem race, multi-process #380 old-client/Service/DB-generation isolation, all managed writer/reader/trigger/FTS source-ID cutover, exact product-linked SQLite 3.51.3 BM25/corpus semantics, representative WAL/disk/reader lease/GC, Windows/macOS native verification, Schema number coordination. None is proven by test-only Python 3.53.1.

### Next gate authorization — D4-S4 TRANSITIVE AUTHORITY AND COMMIT BARRIER (research-only)

Same Codex B may create a **fresh isolated research successor from exact D4-S3 HEAD**. No production/Schema/PR/master mutations. Do **not** redo all S0-S3 investigations or rerun costly CI. Preserve old 15, 7, 4, 16 results and SHA evidence, but focus on:
1. Table/column-level *transitive source-of-truth dependency map* from effective visibility and publication guards through `scan_runs`, root revision/watcher state, `file_sources`, `file_physical_identity_epochs`, `source_identity_claims`, `scan_roots` and `files`/FTS; distinguish sealed membership/identity from separately versioned user metadata. Provide exact writer entry points and authoritative action/transaction owner.
2. A minimal counterexample-first SQLite prototype testing **post-publish evidence change without pointer CAS** (at least run coverage flip, source confidence/status change, identity epoch/digest mutation, claim removal, root metadata change) and direct **digest-mismatch publication bypass**; document expected consequences separately for list results, identity validity and action authorization. If any old mutation is harmless by the explicitly chosen contract, prove that and narrow the gate; do not invent a bug.
3. Add research-only DML guards or a precise immutable-reference/revision fence and a **single trusted publication transaction contract** for digest/count, identity and root map. Prevent invalid direct publish without claiming SQL SHA functions that do not exist. Verify old-candidate-fails / new-candidate-passes and permitted updates in independent user-metadata domain.
4. Verify S3's valid nested-root, rename, cursor, FTS, rollback and existing historical fixtures remain valid. Keep archive hashes and reproducible raw evidence.
5. Specify exact-product SQLite 3.51.3 FTS/BM25 and #380 DB-generation tests as **unexecuted next-stage required gates**, not just an assumption. Do not launch broad perf/Hosted jobs or old-client code changes.

No Codex Review, full CI, Windows/macOS Hosted, benchmarks, merge, Issue closure, release, Schema v38 allocation or PR383/386 changes. At most small offline test-only SQLite harness and evidence. STOP at `#381-D4-S4 READY_FOR_OWNER_TRANSITIVE_AUTHORITY_REVIEW` if proven, else `#381-D4-S4 TRANSITIVE_AUTHORITY_UNRESOLVED`, then Owner reviews. **Both remain production NO-GO.**

**Decision:** `#381-D4-S3 CORE_RELATIONAL_AUTHORITY_ACCEPTED / TRANSITIVE_EVIDENCE_SEAL_UNPROVEN / D4-S4_RESEARCH_ONLY_GO / D4_PRODUCTION_NO_GO`.

### ACCEPTED, restricted to the compatible-service research model

- Existing D4-S2 (15 assertion groups), D4-S3 (7 old counterexamples, 4 illegal publications, 16 mutation refusals) are genuinely invoked by importing/running the frozen D4-S3 runner.
- S4 adds actual 7 transitive evidence-mutation counterexamples and 2 wrong-digest direct SQL publication counterexamples against the S3 prototype. Tested protection SQL covers published `scan_runs` terminal coverage, `file_sources` confidence/status/version, physical identity epochs, identity claims, root/Watcher semantics, current `files.path/name`, Manifest seal and pointer capability.
- For permitted mutations, new `d4s4_effective_file_sources` uses an authority seal/clock; stale visibility and Cursor fail closed while historical rows remain. User file context, display_name and tag updates stay writable.
- `trusted_publish` uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, frozen D3 Oracle, application-side canonical SHA256 and connection-local capability before status/pointer CAS; raw direct publishing with capability false fails. These are **compatible service programming contracts**, not defenses against an older or untrusted SQLite writer able to install its own UDF/drop triggers. #380 DB generation and single-writer barrier is a hard dependency.
- Explicitly retained blockers: native Win/macOS identity, watcher race, exact SQLite 3.51.3 FTS/BM25 semantics, all downstream reader/writer cutover, GC/WAL/disk/reader leases, user DB migration, and #380 installer/old client/service isolation.

### IMPORTANT NEW FINDINGS — NO production schema freeze

**P0 1. Global authority clock causes cross-root outage under ordinary Watcher/root activity.** `d4s4_effective_file_sources` has a single `WHERE seal.authority_revision = clock.revision` on the **whole Manifest**. `scan_roots.watcher_revision` and related operational changes are frequent and trigger the clock. Any change in one root hides **ALL current roots**, including unrelated unaffected files, while pointer remains unchanged, until *all* roots are republished under the new global revision. With recurring Watcher events this can lead to persistent File Library/search unavailability. This is an acceptable intentionally fail-closed **research counterexample**, not an acceptable unqualified production policy. Require root-scoped evidence versioning and affected-source eligibility: an unaffected root remains visible; for one source in overlapping roots, a still-valid owner can retain membership only if its independently verified source/path evidence is consistent; invalid/unresolved identities fail closed **per source/path**, not globally. No source/tag inheritance by same path.

**P0 2. Evidence-mutating writes are not demonstrated atomic.** The original D4-S2 `open_db()` uses `sqlite3.connect(..., isolation_level=None)` (autocommit). D4-S4 `authority_mutation()` executes one statement under a temporarily armed UDF flag, without an explicit surrounding write transaction. In `test_transitive_mutation_guards` claim-revocation code, `UPDATE file_sources SET source_revision=source_revision+1` and `INSERT INTO d4s4_claim_revocations` are **separate autocommitted SQL statements** (runner lines ~558–569); their triggers each advance the global clock, from **1 to 3**, matching committed results. If the second statement fails, the first source version and authority invalidation may already be durable, with no corresponding revoked claim; the code does not test power/process failure between them, rollback, reopen or an independent read connection. A real one-event one-version protocol must wrap revocation + source revision + affected root/source invalidation in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/COMMIT (or equivalent), guarantee exactly one semantic authority advance per logical event (or formally justify a different monotonic rule), test mid-operation injected failure and cross-connection visibility before/after COMMIT. The current prototype proves individually executed fail-closed SQL and same-connection observations, **not** atomic multi-statement evidence mutation.

**P1 3. Evidence archive incomplete on exact Git tree.** `docs/project/research/issue-381-d4-s4/evidence/SHA256SUMS` declares `evidence/transitive-evidence-run.log` digest `674d6a82e1b123e3f5976e1c922df347cd897a0d01d4005f2622550ab79a2782`, but the file is **absent** from all 10 changed paths and exact HEAD GitHub `fetch_file` returns **404**. The accessible results JSON, SQL and runner are sufficient to assess the research result; do not describe the complete 10-file manifest as *remotely archived* until the actual original log is added. Commit the true byte-preserved log if available, or correct evidence provenance/manifest explicitly; do not fabricate a historical run log.

**P1 4. Semantic vs operational revisions and cursor contract.** Schema37 `scan_roots.revision` is a broad admission/lease CAS and cannot be a continuous visibility epoch. The S4 ADR itself recognizes the need to separate semantic root/config revision. A global `authority_revision`-only token cannot give good cross-root availability; specify a root/session-scoped revision vector and query-scope validation while preserving real-time fail closed for invalidated source identity. Do not assume a per-root solution is inherently safe for a source owned by multiple overlapping roots. Existing product consumer `files.is_stale` reads make mixed old/new read path particularly dangerous until migration.

**P1 5. Scope of authorization still depends on trusted connection discipline.** `d4s4_publish_authorized()` is connection-local callback, not cryptographic proof. The test intentionally demonstrates no-function errors and direct SQL failures on a compatible connection; don't claim robustness against raw SQLite with arbitrary UDF registration or schema modification. Define precise Owner-approved #380 generation handshake and single-writer isolation before future production GO.

### NEXT: one focused D4-S5 OFFLINE RESEARCH PHASE, not production

Authorize a **new independent D4-S5 test/document successor from exact S4 HEAD**, with **no production/Schema/PR/master modifications** and no Hosted/full CI/benchmarks:
1. Correct the S4 log/manifest/provenance discrepancy (source log only, no reconstruction).
2. Build a small **two-root/overlap + different-source** counterexample-first SQLite fixture: invalidate A's watcher/root, require B-only unrelated sources stay visible; invalidate source A, require unrelated B sources stay visible; source shared by A and B must remain visible only with verified B-owned membership and matching path/identity; last eligible root loss hides only affected source. Show old global-clock failure, then test a minimal **root-scoped version/seal** candidate with precise active projection/list/FTS visibility and cross-transaction scoped Cursor behavior. Decide between global query-snapshot epoch vs root-filtered Cursors and state the one consistent policy.
3. Test **atomic evidence mutation** for source status, root config, Watcher, claim revocation: explicit transaction, forced failure after each step, rollback, committed reopen on **separate** SQLite connections, pointer and seal preservation, one logical event/one monotonic clock step or documented equivalent. Include revocation of an already-published claim with durable audit trail and negative no-revocation-on-failure result.
4. Preserve previous S2/S3/S4 approved assertions and hashes without rerunning expensive suites unnecessarily; validate only changed minimal synthetic pathways. Keep native identity, SQLite 3.51.3 FTS ranking, #380 generation gate as **unexecuted** separate requirements.
5. Produce revised scoped authority ADR and exact tested HEAD/Tree, raw result/log, SHA256, diff and remaining risk. Stop at `#381-D4-S5 READY_FOR_OWNER_SCOPED_AUTHORITY_REVIEW` if these rules are proven, else `#381-D4-S5 SCOPED_AUTHORITY_UNRESOLVED`.

No Schema v38 reservation, production scanner/FTS/query, installer/IPC/client work, Windows/macOS Hosted, large benchmark, full CI, Codex Review, merge, Issue close or Release. D4-S5 results are **not** production GO; next cross-track integration must await #380 one-writer DB-generation gate.
